maintenance: Release v1.15.0 on 2026-10-23; last commit 2026-10-25
install: Run `npx -y @toolbox-sdk/server --prebuilt=postgres --stdio` (other `--prebuilt` databases in the README), or install the binary and point your MCP client at the local Toolbox HTTP endpoint shown in the README Connect section.
verdict: Pick it to explore schemas and run SQL from the agent across many databases (Postgres, BigQuery, Cloud SQL, Spanner and others); prefer custom toolsets when you need restricted queries in production.

name: Linear MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a setup section in Linear's official MCP docs (linear.app/docs/mcp)
permissions: Finds, creates and updates Linear objects such as issues, projects and comments in your workspace; read-only access via https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly or by requesting only the `read` OAuth scope.
credentials: Linear OAuth 2.1 (interactive flow), or a Linear API key / OAuth token sent as an Authorization: Bearer header.
maintenance: Hosted remote server (MCP Registry app.linear/linear v1.0.2, published 2026-10-22); no public source repository or GitHub release
install: Connect to https://mcp.linear.app/mcp (Streamable HTTP). Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http linear-server https://mcp.linear.app/mcp`, then run `/mcp` to authenticate; Codex: `codex mcp add linear --url https://mcp.linear.app/mcp` (see docs for other clients).
license: Not stated (hosted service, no public source repository)
verdict: Pick it when the agent should read or update Linear issues and projects; use the /mcp/readonly endpoint or the read scope when it only needs to look things up.

name: GitLab MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a "Connect <client> to the GitLab MCP server" section in GitLab's official docs (docs.gitlab.com/user/model_context_protocol/mcp_server)
permissions: Acts on your GitLab data on your behalf: projects, issues/work items, merge requests, repository and CI tools by default (wikis, code_security and orbit toolsets are opt-in); each tool still checks your project and namespace permissions. GitLab warns you are responsible for guarding against prompt injection.
credentials: OAuth access token with the `mcp` scope (dynamic client registration or a pre-registered OAuth app), or a fine-grained personal access token with the MCP tool resource; legacy, project and group tokens are rejected. Access must be allowed for the top-level group (GitLab.com) or the instance.
maintenance: Built into GitLab (generally available since GitLab 19.5, all tiers); MCP server docs last changed 2026-10-17 in gitlab-org/gitlab; no separate release
install: Add the HTTP server `https://gitlab.com/api/v4/mcp` (Self-Managed/Dedicated: `/api/v4/mcp` on your instance URL). Claude Code: `claude mcp add -s user --transport http GitLab https://gitlab.com/api/v4/mcp`; clients without HTTP support use `npx mcp-remote` (see docs).
license: Not stated for the MCP server (built into GitLab)
verdict: Pick it to work with GitLab merge requests, issues and pipelines from the agent; limit toolsets with the X-Gitlab-Enabled-Mcp-Server-Toolsets header for narrower access.

name: Vercel MCP
agentsSource: supported clients list in Vercel's official MCP docs (vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp); Vercel only allows reviewed and approved clients
permissions: Searches Vercel docs, manages projects and deployments, reads deployment logs and queries Web Analytics; Vercel says connecting grants the AI the same access as your Vercel user account (limited by the OAuth grant and team permissions).
credentials: Vercel account OAuth (explicit consent for each client connection).
maintenance: Hosted remote server; official docs last updated 2026-09-15; no public source repository or GitHub release
install: Connect to https://mcp.vercel.com. Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http vercel https://mcp.vercel.com`, then `/mcp` to authenticate; or `npx add-mcp https://mcp.vercel.com` to configure detected clients (see docs).
license: Not stated (hosted service, no public source repository)
verdict: Pick it to inspect deployments and logs or manage Vercel projects from the agent; it acts with your account's access, so keep human confirmation on for changes.

name: Brave Search MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a usage section in the official README (Claude Desktop, VS Code; also the fx terminal agent)
permissions: Sends your search queries to the Brave Search API (web, local, image, video, news, place search, summarizer and LLM context tools); tools can be limited with BRAVE_MCP_ENABLED_TOOLS / BRAVE_MCP_DISABLED_TOOLS.
credentials: BRAVE_API_KEY (or BRAVE_API_KEY_FILE) from a Brave Search API account.
maintenance: Release v2.1.4 on 2026-09-17; last commit 2026-10-21
install: `npx -y @brave/brave-search-mcp-server --transport stdio` with BRAVE_API_KEY, or Docker image `mcp/brave-search` (see README).
verdict: Pick it for web and news search from the agent through Brave's independent index; you need a Brave Search API key and queries go to Brave's API.

name: Exa MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with install buttons, commands or config locations in the official README
permissions: Sends search queries and URLs to Exa's hosted service: web_search_exa and web_fetch_exa by default; agent_run (Exa Agent) and advanced search are opt-in via the `tools` URL parameter.
credentials: Optional: works anonymously with rate limits; Exa OAuth or an Exa API key for higher limits and Exa Agent.
maintenance: Hosted remote server (MCP Registry ai.exa/exa v3.4.1; npm exa-mcp-server 3.4.2 on 2026-10-06); no GitHub release; last commit 2026-10-19
install: Connect to https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp. Claude Code: `claude plugin install exa@claude-plugins-official`; Codex: `codex mcp add exa --url https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp` (see README for other clients).
verdict: Pick it for web search and clean page fetching in the agent without an API key to start; add OAuth or a key for higher limits and multi-step Exa Agent research.

name: Prisma MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a setup section in Prisma's official MCP docs (prisma.io/docs/ai/tools/mcp-server)
permissions: Manages Prisma Postgres databases (create, run SQL, restore backups), Prisma Compute deployments (logs, environment variables), Object Storage buckets and access keys, and searches Prisma docs in the workspace you approve; Prisma warns that tools that change or delete resources can cause data loss.
credentials: Prisma Console account sign-in (OAuth), then pick a workspace and approve access.
maintenance: Hosted remote server; official docs last updated 2026-09-22; the old prisma/mcp repo is archived; no GitHub release
install: Connect to https://mcp.prisma.io/mcp (Streamable HTTP). Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http prisma https://mcp.prisma.io/mcp`; Gemini CLI: `gemini mcp add --transport http Prisma https://mcp.prisma.io/mcp --scope user` (see docs for other clients).
license: Not stated (hosted service, no public source repository)
verdict: Pick it if you run Prisma Postgres or Prisma Compute and want the agent to query data, check backups or read deploy logs; review every destructive approval, it acts on live resources.

name: Tavily MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with setup instructions in the official README (tavily-ai/tavily-mcp)
permissions: Sends search queries and URLs to Tavily's API: tavily-search, tavily-extract, tavily-map and tavily-crawl; no local file access.
credentials: Tavily API key (free tier available) in the URL or an Authorization header, or OAuth on the remote server.
maintenance: npm tavily-mcp v0.2.22; no GitHub release; last commit 2026-10-15
install: Remote: connect to https://mcp.tavily.com/mcp. Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http tavily https://mcp.tavily.com/mcp` (OAuth) or append `?tavilyApiKey=<your-api-key>`; local: `npx -y tavily-mcp@latest` with TAVILY_API_KEY.
verdict: Pick it for real-time web search plus page extraction, site mapping and crawling in one server; needs a Tavily key or OAuth, and every query goes to Tavily.

name: docx
agentsSource: anthropics/skills README (Claude Code, Claude.ai, Claude API)
permissions: Runs local scripts that create, read and edit Word (.docx/.dotx) files, including tracked changes and comments.
credentials: None
maintenance: No GitHub release; last commit 2026-07-17 (path-scoped)
install: Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills`, then `/plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills` (see repo README).
license: Proprietary, source-available (skill LICENSE.txt; not open source)
verdict: Pick it when the agent must produce or edit real Word documents (reports, memos, templates with tracked changes); source-available, not open source.

name: xlsx
agentsSource: anthropics/skills README (Claude Code, Claude.ai, Claude API)
permissions: Runs local scripts that read, create and edit spreadsheet files (.xlsx, .xlsm, .csv, .tsv), including formulas, formatting and charts.

license: Proprietary, source-available (skill LICENSE.txt; not open source)
verdict: Pick it when the deliverable is a spreadsheet: cleaning messy tabular files, adding formulas or charts; source-available, not open source.

name: pptx
agentsSource: anthropics/skills README (Claude Code, Claude.ai, Claude API)
permissions: Runs local scripts that read, create and edit PowerPoint (.pptx/.potx) files, including layouts, speaker notes and comments.
credentials: None
maintenance: No GitHub release; last commit 2026-07-17 (path-scoped)
install: Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills`, then `/plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills` (see repo README).
license: Proprietary, source-available (skill LICENSE.txt; not open source)
verdict: Pick it to build or edit slide decks from the agent, or extract text from existing presentations; source-available, not open source.

name: Shopify Dev MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with a Dev MCP setup section in Shopify's official AI Toolkit docs (shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/ai-toolkit)
permissions: Searches Shopify developer docs and API schemas and validates GraphQL, Liquid themes and UI-extension code blocks against Shopify schemas; runs locally and does not touch a store.
credentials: None (runs locally, no authentication per Shopify's docs); Node.js 18+.
maintenance: npm @shopify/dev-mcp v1.17.0 published 2026-10-16; the Shopify AI Toolkit (plugin + skills) released v2.2.0 the same day
install: Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport stdio shopify-dev-mcp -- npx -y @shopify/dev-mcp@latest`; Cursor/VS Code/Codex: run `npx -y @shopify/dev-mcp@latest` as a stdio server (Shopify also recommends its AI Toolkit plugin, e.g. `claude plugin install shopify-ai-toolkit@claude-plugins-official`).
verdict: Pick it when you build Shopify apps, themes or extensions and want the agent to look up current API docs and validate GraphQL or Liquid before you ship; no store access, no keys.

name: Slack MCP Server
agentsSource: partner clients and harness setup sections in Slack's official docs (docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server)
permissions: Acts as you in Slack with the user-token scopes you grant: searches messages, files, channels and users, reads channels and threads, sends and schedules messages, adds reactions, creates channels, creates and edits canvases and lists, and uploads files.
credentials: Slack OAuth (user token) through a Slack Marketplace or internal app; a workspace admin must approve the MCP integration.
maintenance: Hosted remote server (no public source); official Slack plugin slackapi/slack-skills-plugin released v1.5.0 on 2026-10-19
install: Connect to https://mcp.slack.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth). Claude Code: `/plugin install slack@claude-plugins-official` (recommended) or `claude mcp add --transport http --scope local slack https://mcp.slack.com/mcp`, then `/mcp`; Codex: `codex mcp add --transport http slack https://mcp.slack.com/mcp`.
license: Not stated (hosted service; the MIT slack-skills-plugin repo only holds the client plugin)
verdict: Pick it when the agent should find past decisions in Slack or post updates and canvases for you; it can send messages as you, so grant only the scopes you need and keep admin approval on.

name: Asana MCP Server (V2)
agentsSource: clients with setup sections in Asana's official developer docs (developers.asana.com, Using Asana's MCP Server and Connecting Coding Clients to the V2 server)
permissions: Reads and writes your Asana work graph within your account's permissions: finds tasks, creates and assigns tasks and projects, lists sections, and reports on project status.
credentials: Asana OAuth 2.0 with a pre-registered Asana MCP app (client ID and secret); Enterprise+ admins can allow or block each client.
maintenance: Hosted remote server (no public source repository); client setup docs last modified 2026-08-02; the V1 beta endpoint (mcp.asana.com/sse) is deprecated
install: Connect to https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth). Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http --client-id YOUR_CLIENT_ID --client-secret --callback-port 8080 asana https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp`; Cursor: url plus auth CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET (see docs for other clients).
license: Not stated (hosted service, no public source repository)
verdict: Pick it when the agent should read or create Asana tasks and projects; you first register an Asana MCP app for the client ID and secret, and Asana warns that the mcp-remote bridge some clients need is unofficial.

name: Hugging Face MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with an install section in the official README (huggingface/hf-mcp-server)
permissions: Searches and reads Hub models, datasets, Spaces, papers and docs; optional tools you enable in your MCP settings can create and write repos, run and schedule Jobs, use sandboxes, and call Gradio Spaces as tools.
credentials: Hugging Face account sign-in (OAuth via ?login) or a Hugging Face token in an Authorization: Bearer header.
maintenance: Release v0.4.31 on 2026-10-19; last commit 2026-10-24
install: Remote: connect to https://huggingface.co/mcp. Claude Code: `claude mcp add hf-mcp-server -t http https://huggingface.co/mcp?login` (or `-H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_HF_TOKEN>"`); then pick tools and Spaces at huggingface.co/settings/mcp.
verdict: Pick it to find models, datasets, Spaces and docs on the Hub from your agent; keep write tools (repos, Jobs) off unless you need them, they act on your HF account.

name: Zapier MCP
agentsSource: clients listed in Zapier's official MCP quickstart (docs.zapier.com/mcp) and the zapier/zapier-mcp README
permissions: Runs the Zapier actions you enable (or, in agentic mode, that the agent finds and enables) across 9,000+ apps through your own Zapier app connections: send messages and emails, create tasks, update records, search data.
credentials: Zapier account via OAuth from the client; code integrations and unlisted clients use a long-lived connection token. Each successful tool call uses two tasks from your Zapier plan.
maintenance: Hosted remote server (MCP Registry com.zapier/mcp v1.0.1, published 2026-07-29); plugin repo zapier/zapier-mcp last commit 2026-07-29; no GitHub release
install: Connect to https://mcp.zapier.com/api/v1/connect (Streamable HTTP, OAuth). Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http "Zapier-MCP" https://mcp.zapier.com/api/v1/connect`, restart and sign in; VS Code: add the URL as type http (see docs for other clients).
license: Not stated (hosted service; the MIT zapier/zapier-mcp repo only holds the client plugin)
verdict: Pick it when the agent needs to act in apps that have no MCP server of their own; prefer managed mode with a fixed action list, and remember every call spends Zapier tasks.

name: Postman MCP Server
agentsSource: clients in the Supported agents and IDEs table of the official README (postmanlabs/postman-mcp-server) and Postman's remote-server docs
permissions: Reads and changes your Postman workspaces, collections, specs, environments and variables (create, tag, update, comment) and generates client code from API definitions; Minimal (default), Code, Full (100+ tools), Learn and Context Graph tool sets.
credentials: Postman account via OAuth on the US remote server; the EU remote server and the local server need a Postman API key (POSTMAN_API_KEY or Authorization: Bearer header).
maintenance: Release v2.14.0 on 2026-10-16 (npm @postman/postman-mcp-server 2.14.0); last commit 2026-10-16
install: Remote: connect to https://mcp.postman.com/minimal (or /code, /mcp for Full). Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http postman https://mcp.postman.com/minimal`; Cursor/VS Code: add the URL (VS Code type http). Local: `npx @postman/postman-mcp-server` with POSTMAN_API_KEY (add --code or --full).
verdict: Pick it when your API collections and specs live in Postman and you want the agent to keep them in sync with code; start with Minimal, and use the local server to test APIs on your machine.

name: Snyk MCP Server (Snyk Studio)
agentsSource: Snyk Studio quickstart guides in the official docs (docs.snyk.io, Agent security > Quickstart guides)
permissions: Runs Snyk scans on local folders you trust: SAST (snyk_code_scan), open-source dependencies (snyk_sca_scan, may run Maven/Gradle etc. to build the dependency tree), containers, IaC, SBOM and AI-BOM, package health; results are sent back to the agent.
credentials: Snyk account; authenticate on first use with the snyk_auth tool (browser sign-in) and trust the project folder with snyk_trust. Node.js/npx or the Snyk CLI installed.
maintenance: Ships inside the Snyk CLI: release v1.1308.3 on 2026-10-23 (npm snyk 1.1308.3); snyk/studio-mcp v1.15.6 on 2026-10-21
install: Local only (Snyk offers no hosted remote server). Any client: stdio server `npx -y snyk@latest mcp -t stdio` (optional `--profile=lite`). Claude Code shortcut: `npx -y snyk@latest mcp configure --tool=claude-cli`; hooks-based Snyk Studio installer for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and Copilot (see docs).
license: Apache-2.0 (Snyk CLI LICENSE; scans use the Snyk service under your plan)
verdict: Pick it to have the agent scan the code and dependencies it just wrote before you commit; use the lite profile to save tokens, and only trust folders you mean to scan.

name: Auth0 MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with install steps in the official README (auth0/auth0-mcp-server)
permissions: Manages your Auth0 tenant: lists, creates and updates applications, APIs (resource servers) and client grants, creates and deploys Actions, reads logs, manages forms; `--read-only` or `--tools` patterns limit the tools, and secrets are redacted in responses.
credentials: Auth0 account via OAuth 2.0 device authorization (`init` opens the browser); credentials stored in the system keychain. Private Cloud tenants use client credentials of an M2M app.
maintenance: Beta: pre-release v0.1.0-beta.19 on 2026-08-13 (npm @auth0/auth0-mcp-server 0.1.0-beta.19); README marks it not recommended for production
install: Run `npx @auth0/auth0-mcp-server init --client <claude-code|cursor|vscode|windsurf|gemini>` (Claude Desktop: `init` alone); add `--read-only` to expose only read tools. Other clients: stdio `npx -y @auth0/auth0-mcp-server run`.
verdict: Pick it to set up Auth0 apps, APIs and Actions or debug login logs from your editor; it is beta, so start with --read-only and point it at a dev tenant.

name: CircleCI MCP Server (hosted)
agentsSource: clients with setup tabs in CircleCI's official docs (Connecting to the CircleCI MCP server)
permissions: Lists and reads your CircleCI runs, workflows, jobs, step logs, artifacts and test results, exports org usage data, and can rerun (from start or from failed) or cancel workflows.
credentials: CircleCI account via OAuth2 from the client; hosts that cannot do OAuth use a CircleCI personal API token.
maintenance: Hosted remote server; setup docs last updated 2026-09-28. Replaces the deprecated local @circleci/mcp-server-circleci (npm 0.20.0, repo to be archived). The CircleCI CLI (v1.11.0, 2026-10-21) can also expose its commands as a local MCP server (`circleci mcp`).
install: Connect to https://mcp.circleci.com/v1/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth2). Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http circleci-mcp-server https://mcp.circleci.com/v1/mcp`, then /mcp > Authenticate; Claude and Cursor: add CircleCI from their directories; VS Code: type http.
verdict: Pick it to ask why the last CircleCI run failed and get the logs and failing tests in your editor; review reruns and cancels before approving, they change real CI state.

name: LaunchDarkly MCP Server (hosted)
agentsSource: clients with manual setup steps in LaunchDarkly's official hosted MCP docs
permissions: Creates, reads, updates and deletes feature flags and AgentControl configs and reads observability data (logs, traces, errors, sessions) with the role of the member who authorized it; returned data (contexts, member emails, server-side SDK keys) goes to your model provider.
credentials: LaunchDarkly account via OAuth (access tokens last two hours, reauthorize every 90 days). EU and federal instances need the local server (npm @launchdarkly/mcp-server) with an API access token.
maintenance: Hosted remote server; local server for EU/federal released v0.7.1 on 2026-10-21 (npm @launchdarkly/mcp-server 0.7.1)
install: Connect to https://mcp.launchdarkly.com/mcp/launchdarkly (Streamable HTTP, OAuth), or use the install page https://mcp.launchdarkly.com/mcp/launchdarkly/install. Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http "launchdarkly" "https://mcp.launchdarkly.com/mcp/launchdarkly"`; Cursor: add the URL in .cursor/mcp.json and click Connect.
license: Not stated (hosted service; the local server repo launchdarkly/mcp-server is MIT)
verdict: Pick it to create and roll out feature flags from your editor; connect as a member with the smallest role you need and never auto-approve flag changes in production.

name: Pinecone Developer MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with setup steps in Pinecone's official MCP docs (docs.pinecone.io) and the official README
permissions: Searches Pinecone docs; with an API key it lists and describes indexes, creates indexes with integrated embedding, upserts records, searches and reranks across indexes in the project the key belongs to. Only indexes with integrated embedding are supported.
credentials: Optional: works without a key for docs search only; a Pinecone API key (PINECONE_API_KEY) is needed to manage or query indexes. Node.js 20+ with npx.
maintenance: Official repo pinecone-io/pinecone-mcp; release v0.3.0 on 2026-08-07 (npm @pinecone-database/mcp 0.3.0); last push 2026-10-22
install: Local stdio server `npx -y @pinecone-database/mcp` with PINECONE_API_KEY in env. Claude Code: `claude mcp add-json pinecone-mcp '{"type":"stdio","command":"npx","args":["-y","@pinecone-database/mcp"],"env":{"PINECONE_API_KEY":"YOUR_API_KEY"}}'`; Cursor: same command in .cursor/mcp.json; Gemini CLI: `gemini extensions install https://github.com/pinecone-io/pinecone-mcp`.
verdict: Pick it to prototype RAG and semantic search on Pinecone from your editor; use a key for a dev project only, since the agent can create indexes and upsert data.

name: JetBrains IDE MCP Server (built-in)
agentsSource: clients with auto-configuration listed in JetBrains' official MCP Server docs (IntelliJ IDEA help); others via copied SSE, stdio or HTTP config
permissions: Gives connected clients access to the projects open in the IDE: read, create and patch files, search, inspections and builds, run configurations, debugger control, refactorings, Git status, terminal commands and (with the Database Tools plugin) SQL queries. Terminal commands and run configurations ask for confirmation unless brave mode is on; each tool can be disabled.
credentials: None: runs locally inside a JetBrains IDE 2025.2+ (bundled MCP Server plugin); enable it in Settings | Tools | MCP Server. Some database tools need a paid plan.
maintenance: Built into IntelliJ-based IDEs since 2025.2 (bundled plugin com.intellij.mcpServer); IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2.3 released 2026-09-16. The old JetBrains/mcp-jetbrains npm proxy is deprecated and not listed.
install: In the IDE: Settings | Tools | MCP Server → Enable MCP Server → Apply, then click Auto-Configure for your client (Claude Code, Codex, VS Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Junie) or use Copy SSE / Stdio / HTTP Stream Config for any other client and restart it.
license: Proprietary (ships with JetBrains IDEs under their license)
verdict: Pick it to let a terminal agent use your IDE's inspections, builds, refactorings and debugger; keep brave mode off and disable tools you don't need.

name: Apify MCP Server
agentsSource: tested clients in the official README (apify/apify-mcp-server) and clients named in docs.apify.com/mcp
permissions: Searches Apify Store and runs Actors (scrapers, crawlers, automations) on your account, reads datasets, key-value stores and run results, and searches Apify docs; extra tools (e.g. delete-actor) only when selected with `tools=`. Full-permission Actors are excluded. Actor runs consume Apify usage credits.
credentials: Apify account via OAuth on the hosted server (or an Apify API token as Bearer header / APIFY_TOKEN for local stdio); agentic payments (x402, Skyfire) are an alternative for some Actors.
maintenance: Official repo apify/apify-mcp-server; release v0.19.3 on 2026-10-21 (npm @apify/actors-mcp-server 0.19.3); last commit 2026-10-25; hosted at https://mcp.apify.com
install: Connect to https://mcp.apify.com (Streamable HTTP, OAuth). Generate a client-specific config at https://mcp.apify.com or run `apify mcp install cursor` with the Apify CLI. Local: `npx -y @apify/actors-mcp-server` with APIFY_TOKEN. Coding agents can use the Apify plugin (server + Agent Skills).
verdict: Pick it when the agent needs ready-made scrapers for sites like Google Maps, Instagram or e-commerce; limit the loaded tools with `tools=` and watch Actor run costs.

name: Perplexity API Platform MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with install buttons, commands or config locations in the official README (perplexityai/modelcontextprotocol)
permissions: Sends your prompts to Perplexity's API: perplexity_search (web results), perplexity_ask, perplexity_reason and perplexity_research (Agent API presets; research runs can take minutes). Usage is billed to your API key.
credentials: Perplexity API key from console.perplexity.ai (Bearer header on the remote server, PERPLEXITY_API_KEY for the local server).
maintenance: Official repo perplexityai/modelcontextprotocol; no GitHub release, npm @perplexity-ai/mcp-server 1.3.0 on 2026-09-25; last push 2026-10-21; hosted at https://api.perplexity.ai/mcp
install: Remote: connect to https://api.perplexity.ai/mcp with your API key. Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http perplexity https://api.perplexity.ai/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"`. Local: `npx -y @perplexity-ai/mcp-server` with PERPLEXITY_API_KEY (Codex: `codex mcp add perplexity --env PERPLEXITY_API_KEY=... -- npx -y @perplexity-ai/mcp-server`).
verdict: Pick it for cited, up-to-date web answers and deep research inside the agent; reserve perplexity_research for big questions, since it is slower and costs more.

name: PostHog MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with setup guides in PostHog's official MCP docs (posthog.com/docs/model-context-protocol)
permissions: Reads and writes across your PostHog project with your account's access: product analytics and HogQL/SQL queries, error tracking (stack traces, issue status), feature flags, experiments, surveys, CDP destinations and more. Add `readonly=true` to drop all write tools; pin to one project with x-posthog-project-id.
credentials: PostHog account via OAuth (routes to US or EU automatically), or a personal API key with the MCP Server preset as a Bearer header.
maintenance: Hosted remote server (free to call; some AI-powered tools bill as PostHog AI spend); source in PostHog/posthog services/mcp, last commit 2026-10-26. The old PostHog/mcp repo is archived.
install: Connect to https://mcp.posthog.com/mcp (OAuth). Wizard for most clients: `npx @posthog/wizard mcp add`. Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http posthog https://mcp.posthog.com/mcp -s user` or `claude plugin install posthog`.
license: MIT (services/mcp package; hosted service under PostHog terms)
verdict: Pick it to triage production errors and check feature flags or analytics from your editor; start with readonly=true and pin the project before allowing writes.

name: Upstash MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with setup snippets in Upstash's official MCP docs (upstash.com/docs/agent-resources/mcp) and the upstash/mcp-server README
permissions: Manages your Upstash account across Redis, QStash, Workflow, Vector, Search, Box and Blob: lists and creates databases and indexes, runs Redis commands, reads stats, logs and the DLQ, and can change plans, budgets, reset credentials or delete resources (74 tools on the hosted server). A read-only OAuth grant or read-only API key disables every write/destructive tool; `?features=` limits which product tools load. Plan and budget tools change billing.
credentials: Upstash account via OAuth on the hosted server (choose personal/team scope and read-only at consent), or a Developer API key as `Authorization: Bearer email:API_KEY` for headless use; the legacy local server takes --email and --api-key.
maintenance: Hosted remote server at https://mcp.upstash.com/mcp is the recommended option; official repo upstash/mcp-server, release v0.4.0 on 2026-10-23. The README says the local stdio package @upstash/mcp-server is no longer maintained.
install: Connect to https://mcp.upstash.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth). Claude Code: `claude mcp add --scope user --transport http upstash https://mcp.upstash.com/mcp`, then `/mcp` → Authenticate. Cursor: `{"mcpServers":{"upstash":{"url":"https://mcp.upstash.com/mcp"}}}`. Scope tools with e.g. `?features=redis,qstash_workflow`.
license: MIT (upstash/mcp-server; hosted service under Upstash terms)
verdict: Pick it to inspect and debug Upstash Redis, QStash and Workflow from your editor; use the hosted server with a read-only grant first and scope it with ?features=.

name: Okta Open Source MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with config examples in the official README (okta/okta-mcp-server); other MCP clients via the generic stdio config
permissions: Calls Okta Admin Management APIs on your org: CRUD on users, groups, applications, policies, device assurance policies, brands, themes, email templates and domains, plus system log queries. Only tools whose OAuth scopes are in OKTA_SCOPES are loaded (e.g. `okta.users.read okta.groups.read` for read-only); deletes and deactivations ask for confirmation via MCP elicitation. Consumes Management API rate limits.
credentials: An Okta org plus an Okta API service app: OKTA_ORG_URL, OKTA_CLIENT_ID and OKTA_SCOPES, using Device Authorization Grant (browser login, tokens in the system keyring) or Private Key JWT (OKTA_PRIVATE_KEY + OKTA_KEY_ID) for browserless use.
maintenance: Generally available; official repo okta/okta-mcp-server, release v1.1.7 on 2026-09-29 (PyPI okta-mcp-server 1.1.7); documented at developer.okta.com. Okta also offers a separate Okta Managed MCP Server.
install: With uv: stdio command `uvx okta-mcp-server` (Python 3.13+) with env OKTA_ORG_URL, OKTA_CLIENT_ID, OKTA_SCOPES (add OKTA_PRIVATE_KEY/OKTA_KEY_ID for Private Key JWT). Docker (recommended in README): clone the repo, `docker-compose up -d`, then point the client at `docker run -i --rm ... okta-mcp-server`. Pin versions with `okta-mcp-server@1.1.7`.
verdict: Pick it to audit users, groups, apps and sign-in logs in an Okta org from your agent; grant only read scopes in OKTA_SCOPES and try it on a preview/dev org first.

name: Mapbox MCP Server
agentsSource: clients in Mapbox's official docs (docs.mapbox.com/location-ai) and setup guides in the mapbox/mcp-server repo
permissions: Calls Mapbox APIs with your account: geocoding and POI/category search, directions, travel-time matrices, route optimization, map matching, isochrones, static map images and an interactive map renderer (render_map_tool), plus offline geospatial calculations (distance, area, buffers). Read-only toward your data; API calls count against your Mapbox usage and pricing.
credentials: Mapbox account via OAuth on the hosted endpoint, or a Mapbox access token (Bearer header on the hosted server, MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN for the local npm server).
maintenance: Official repo mapbox/mcp-server, release v0.16.0 on 2026-10-15 (npm @mapbox/mcp-server 0.16.0); hosted at https://mcp.mapbox.com/mcp
install: Connect to https://mcp.mapbox.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth). Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http mapbox-mcp-production https://mcp.mapbox.com/mcp`, then `/mcp`. Cursor: `{"mcpServers":{"mapbox-mcp":{"url":"https://mcp.mapbox.com/mcp"}}}`. Local: `npx -y @mapbox/mcp-server` with MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN.
verdict: Pick it when you build location features (geocoding, routing, isochrones, maps) and want the agent to test real Mapbox calls; use a scoped token and watch API usage.

name: ClickHouse MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with setup steps in ClickHouse's official docs (clickhouse.com/docs remote MCP and MCP guides) and the ClickHouse/mcp-clickhouse README
permissions: Open-source server: lists databases and tables and runs SQL via run_query, read-only by default (writes only if CLICKHOUSE_ALLOW_WRITE_ACCESS=true); optional chDB tool queries files/URLs locally. Cloud remote server: list databases/tables, inspect schemas and run read-only SELECTs, plus service, backup, ClickPipes and billing tools, scoped to what your user or API key can access.
credentials: Open-source: ClickHouse connection settings (CLICKHOUSE_HOST, CLICKHOUSE_USER, CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD, optional role). Cloud remote: ClickHouse Cloud OAuth or a Cloud API key via HTTP Basic auth; MCP must be enabled per service.
maintenance: Official repo ClickHouse/mcp-clickhouse, release v0.7.0 on 2026-09-21 (PyPI mcp-clickhouse 0.7.0), last commit 2026-10-21; managed remote server at https://mcp.clickhouse.cloud/mcp for ClickHouse Cloud
install: Self-hosted or any ClickHouse: stdio `uv run --with mcp-clickhouse --python 3.12 mcp-clickhouse` with CLICKHOUSE_HOST/PORT/USER/PASSWORD and CLICKHOUSE_SECURE=true. ClickHouse Cloud: enable MCP under Connect → MCP, then e.g. `claude mcp add --transport http clickhouse-cloud https://mcp.clickhouse.cloud/mcp`.
verdict: Pick it to let the agent explore schemas and write analytical SQL against ClickHouse; keep write access off and connect with a read-only database user.

name: Resend MCP Server
agentsSource: clients with setup steps in the official README (resend/resend-mcp) and resend.com/docs/mcp-server
permissions: Acts on your Resend account: sends, schedules, cancels and batch-sends emails (with attachments), reads received emails and inboxes, and manages templates, contacts, broadcasts, automations, domains, segments, suppressions, topics and API keys. Sending and broadcasts reach real recipients.
credentials: Resend account via OAuth on the hosted server, or a Resend API key (Bearer header remotely, RESEND_API_KEY locally); sending needs a verified domain (optional default SENDER_EMAIL_ADDRESS).
maintenance: Official repo resend/resend-mcp, release v2.27.1 on 2026-10-16 (npm resend-mcp 2.27.1); hosted at https://mcp.resend.com/mcp running the same open-source code
install: Connect to https://mcp.resend.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth). Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http resend https://mcp.resend.com/mcp`, then `/mcp`. Codex: `codex mcp add resend --url https://mcp.resend.com/mcp`. Local: `npx -y resend-mcp` with RESEND_API_KEY.
verdict: Pick it to build and test transactional email flows (templates, domains, test sends) from your editor; use a restricted API key and a test domain, since sends go to real inboxes.

name: Railway MCP Server
agentsSource: editors supported by `railway mcp install` in the official Railway CLI (railwayapp/cli) and hosts named in docs.railway.com/reference/mcp-server
permissions: Acts on your Railway account: lists and creates projects and services, deploys templates, pulls variables, redeploys services, sets and deletes feature flags and can hand multi-step work (logs, debugging, config) to Railway's own agent; the local mode also manages domains, volumes, buckets, TCP proxies and variables. Destructive tools are marked for client confirmation.
credentials: Railway account: the CLI proxy reuses your `railway login` session (no token in the editor config), or OAuth directly against https://mcp.railway.com with per-workspace/project scoping. Project tokens are not accepted.
maintenance: Hosted server at mcp.railway.com, connected through the Railway CLI (needs CLI 5.44.0+; latest v5.71.0 on 2026-10-19). Replaces the archived railwayapp/railway-mcp-server repo.
install: With the Railway CLI: `railway setup agent` (or `railway setup agent --oauth`), or `railway mcp install` to write the config into your editors; `railway mcp` proxies the hosted server over stdio. OAuth clients can connect straight to https://mcp.railway.com without the CLI; offline/egress-restricted: `railway mcp local`.
license: MIT (Railway CLI, which ships the `railway mcp` proxy and local server); hosted server under Railway terms
verdict: Pick it to create, deploy and debug Railway services from your editor without pasting tokens; review redeploy and accept-deploy calls, and keep it off production projects where you can.

name: Render MCP Server (hosted)
agentsSource: client tabs and "other apps" links in Render's official docs (render.com/docs/mcp-server)
permissions: Acts on the selected Render workspace: creates web services, static sites, cron jobs, Render Postgres and Key Value; lists services; updates all environment variables of a service; triggers deploys; reads logs and metrics; runs read-only SQL on Render Postgres. No deletes or scaling changes.
credentials: Render account via OAuth (official plugins for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor; Claude Desktop connector), or a Render API key as an Authorization: Bearer header. The API key grants access to all your workspaces and services.
maintenance: Hosted server at https://mcp.render.com/mcp, auto-updated by Render; open-source code render-oss/render-mcp-server (Apache-2.0), last commit 2026-10-23; last GitHub release v0.3.0 on 2026-01-14 (for local runs, which Render discourages)
install: Connect to https://mcp.render.com/mcp. Claude Code: `/plugin install render@claude-plugins-official`, or `claude mcp add --transport http render https://mcp.render.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>"`; Codex: `codex mcp add render --url https://mcp.render.com/mcp --oauth-client-id codex`; Cursor: `/add-plugin render`. Then tell the agent which Render workspace to use.
license: Apache-2.0 (render-oss/render-mcp-server); hosted service under Render terms
verdict: Pick it to spin up Render services, check deploys and read logs or metrics from the agent; it can rewrite env vars and trigger deploys, so review those calls.

name: Azure DevOps MCP Server
agentsSource: supported environments in Microsoft Learn (remote server) and client sections of docs/GETTINGSTARTED.md in microsoft/azure-devops-mcp (local server)
permissions: Reads and changes Azure DevOps data you can access: projects and teams, work items and queries, repos, branches, pull requests and comments, pipelines (including queuing runs), wikis, test plans and Advanced Security alerts. Remote server supports `X-MCP-Readonly` and toolset/tool filtering headers; local server loads domains with `-d`.
credentials: Microsoft Entra ID (OAuth) for the remote server; Cursor and Claude Code need a custom Entra app registration, Claude Desktop and Codex must use the local server. Local server: interactive Microsoft sign-in, Azure CLI, credential chain, bearer token or PAT.
maintenance: Remote server https://mcp.dev.azure.com/{organization} (preview, recommended by Microsoft); local server release v2.11.0 on 2026-10-22 (npm @azure-devops/mcp 2.11.0); last commit 2026-10-22
install: Remote (VS Code): add `{"servers":{"ado-remote-mcp":{"url":"https://mcp.dev.azure.com/{organization}","type":"http"}}}` to .vscode/mcp.json; Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http ado https://mcp.dev.azure.com/{organization} --client-id {client-id} --callback-port 3118`. Local: `npx -y @azure-devops/mcp {organization}` (optionally `-d core work work-items`).
verdict: Pick it when your team lives in Azure DevOps and you want the agent to read work items, PRs and pipeline logs; start with X-MCP-Readonly and narrow toolsets, since writes act as you.

name: monday.com MCP
agentsSource: clients with setup steps or integration guides linked in the official README (mondaycom/mcp)
permissions: Acts on your monday.com account: creates, updates, moves and deletes items, adds updates, creates boards, groups and columns (and deletes columns), reads board schemas, users and teams, creates and reads forms. Local server has `--read-only`; optional beta Dynamic API Tools give full GraphQL API access.
credentials: monday.com account via OAuth on the hosted server (install the monday MCP app for workspace controls); local server needs a personal API token (MONDAY_TOKEN or `-t`).
maintenance: Hosted server at https://mcp.monday.com/mcp (recommended in the README); official repo mondaycom/mcp, npm @mondaydotcomorg/monday-api-mcp 3.3.1 on 2026-09-22; no GitHub release; last commit 2026-10-26
install: Hosted: add `{"mcpServers":{"monday-mcp":{"url":"https://mcp.monday.com/mcp"}}}` (Cursor) or `gemini mcp add -t http monday https://mcp.monday.com/mcp` then `/mcp auth monday`. Local: `npx @mondaydotcomorg/monday-api-mcp@latest` with MONDAY_TOKEN (add `--read-only` to only read).
verdict: Pick it to turn agent work into monday.com items and status updates, or to summarise sprints from boards; use read-only or limited workspaces first, item and column deletes are permanent.

name: Angular CLI MCP Server
agentsSource: host configurations shown in the official Angular docs (angular.dev/ai/mcp)
permissions: Runs inside your Angular workspace: lists projects from angular.json, starts and stops `ng serve`, runs configured targets (build, test, lint, e2e, deploy), plans OnPush/zoneless migrations, and searches angular.dev docs and best practices. `--read-only` registers only non-modifying tools; `--local-only` skips tools that need internet.
credentials: None (local stdio server via npx; Node.js and an Angular workspace).
maintenance: Ships inside the official Angular CLI: release v22.2.4 on 2026-10-22 (npm @angular/cli 22.2.4); angular/angular-cli last commit 2026-10-26
install: Run `npx -y @angular/cli mcp` as a stdio server, e.g. in .cursor/mcp.json or .vscode/mcp.json: `"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@angular/cli", "mcp"]` (append `--read-only` to block changes).
verdict: Pick it when the agent works on an Angular app and should use current Angular APIs, run builds and tests itself, and follow version-matched best practices; start with --read-only if you only want docs and analysis.
